title: In 13 CMIP6 models, North Pacific outcrop size does not predict projected sigma0 26.5 O2 loss; off California low model O2 makes the projected loss too small; no model gives the observed eastern loss
abstract: Question: earlier work found an O2 loss on the sigma0 26.5 surface across the North Pacific that began where the winter outcrop of the 26.4-26.7 class shrank, and that most CMIP6 models have too small an outcrop. Does the outcrop bias change the projected loss? Approach: 13 CMIP6 Earth system models (historical, SSP2-4.5; 12 also SSP5-8.5), September interior and January-April surface fields read through ESGF OPeNDAP; outcrop area, O2 on sigma0 26.5 and 200-500 m O2; a plan with a primary test hashed before any model value. Results: the 1965-1984 outcrop area did not predict the SSP2-4.5 change of O2 on 26.5 in 25-45 N, 140 E-120 W (Spearman rho -0.15, p 0.31; families +0.02; ensemble -30.7 +/- 13.1 umol/kg). Models with little or no outcrop lost as much O2 as models with a large one; the basin-wide loss followed projected surface lightening (rho -0.56). At 200-500 m there was no relation. Off California the relation was strong: models with little outcrop have 6-11 umol/kg O2 on 26.5 there (GLODAP 94) and project almost no loss. Mean-state O2 predicted the CalCOFI-box change (rho -0.80, Holm p 0.033). An exploratory constraint at the observed O2 gives -19.9 umol/kg (90% interval -31.2 to -8.5) against the raw ensemble mean -11.6 (SSP5-8.5: -25.1 against -13.1). No model gave the observed 1984-1996 to 2009-2025 loss at 150-160 W (-26.0) or at CalCOFI (-24.6): models gave +1.9 to -13.8 and +0.5 to -12.2, and 12 of 13 do not reach the CalCOFI loss by 2081-2100. At the source region, model O2 change followed each model's own surface lightening (rho -0.77), and most models lightened less than observed. Limitations: 13 models, one member each, September samples, exploratory status of the California constraint, and approximate box and variable matches with the observations.

Orange: WOA23 outcrop.

(a) Model and observed O2 change on sigma0 26.5 in the observed windows: no model reaches the observed loss at 150-160 W or at CalCOFI. (b) At 36-46 N, 160 E-180, model O2 change follows each model's own surface lightening; orange: observation.

(a) CalCOFI box: model mean O2 on sigma0 26.5 (1985-2014) predicts the projected change; models near GLODAP lose about 15-25 umol/kg. (b) Basin-wide projected loss follows projected surface lightening.

citations.reason: Outcrop mask and metrics code, WOA23 outcrop areas and March box density used as observed values; we test whether its mean-state result extends to projections.

ESGF index and OPeNDAP fetch code and isopycnal routine reused; our GFDL-ESM4 series reproduce its published series; our cross-model result agrees with its finding that the interior response to lightening occurs without an outcrop.
Its proposal that missing model outcrops may explain why models miss the loss holds off California but not for the basin-wide projected loss in 13 models.
Observed WOD ship O2 changes on sigma0 26.5 in the 150-160 W band and the CalCOFI band (1984-1996 to 2009-2025).
Observed within-type O2 change at 36-46 N, 160 E-180 (1975-1989 to 2007-2025).
The eastern O2 loss being decades ahead of the models agrees with its 35-40 year lead of the observed outcrop loss.
Projected basin-wide O2 loss follows projected surface lightening across models, as its shift law implies.
